title: fmrilatent
text: R package latent space representations fMRI neuroimaging data. Provides S4 classes (LatentNeuroVec) memory-efficient storage manipulation dimensionality-reduced brain data using matrix factorization (basis x loadings). Integrates neuroim2 package standard neuroimaging data structures. core idea: represent 4D fMRI data X = B * L' + c B temporal basis, L spatial loadings, c voxel-wise offset. enables efficient PCA, ICA, wavelet, Slepian, HRBF, decompositions.

title: SlepianEtc Notes
text: Slepian/DPSS: BOLD band-limited; DPSS maximizes energy concentration target bandwidth/region, giving physics-informed compression denoising versus PCA variance-bases. Two modes Temporal Slepian → LatentNeuroVec: fixed DPSS dictionary B (time × k) derived TR bandwidth; voxel loadings L found projection. Reconstruction: X ≈ B_dpss %*% t(L); automatically removes high-frequency physio noise. Spatiotemporal Graph Slepian → ImplicitLatent: temporal DPSS plus spatial graph eigenmodes (smallest Laplacian eigenvalues) respecting voxel adjacency/ROI topology. Reconstruction: X ≈ B_dpss %*% C_core %*% t(U_graph); strong compression ROIs computationally heavier. DPSS generation (avoid heavy deps): implement tridiagonal eigen-solver RcppEigen. code: slepian_temporal_latent <- function(X, mask, tr, bandwidth = 0.1, k = NULL) {   n_time <- nrow(X)   W  <- bandwidth * tr           # normalized half-bandwidth   NW <- n_time * W                # time-bandwidth product   if (is.null(k)) k <- max(1, floor(2 * NW) - 1)  # Shannon number    B <- generate_dpss_basis_rcpp(n_time, NW, k)    # orthogonal DPSS basis   L <- Matrix::crossprod(X, B)                    # loadings (voxels × k)    LatentNeuroVec(     basis    = Matrix::Matrix(B),     loadings = Matrix::Matrix(L),     space    = neuroim2::space(mask),     mask     = mask,     offset   = colMeans(X),     meta     = list(family = "slepian_temporal", tr = tr, bandwidth = bandwidth, nw = NW)   ) }

title: SlepianEtc Notes
text: Core hurdle: full-brain spatial Slepian (≈1e5 voxels) naive eigensolve O(N^3); need sparsity/locality tricks. Approach 1 — Cluster-Slepian (recommended): parcel mask (e.g., Schaefer 400 K-means) ~500–1000 clusters; parcel solve tiny Laplacian eigenproblem (k_per_cluster = 1 gives parcel mean; 2–5 adds gradients). Assemble block-diagonal sparse L; temporal basis B <- X %*% L; yields LatentNeuroVec sparse loadings natural “lifting” (voxel signal → smooth parcel modes). Approach 2 — Nyström: pick ~5% voxels landmarks, solve eigenproblem (~5k nodes), extend eigenvectors remaining voxels via Nyström/interpolation (HRBF/linear); optionally threshold sparsify L; keeps smooth whole-brain gradients without hard parcel boundaries. Approach 3 — Tensor-product lattice: assume regular 3D grid; take Kronecker 1D Slepians/DCT along x/y/z, mask non-brain voxels; avoids eigendecomp entirely, extreme speed regular grids. Helper idea: lift_parcellation(parcellation, mask, k=3) builds sparse block-diagonal lifting matrix (per-parcel eigenmodes) reuse across runs.
code: slepian_cluster_latent <- function(X, mask, clusters, k_per_cluster = 3, tr, bw) {   cluster_ids <- sort(unique(clusters[clusters > 0]))   i <- j <- x <- list(); col_off <- 0   for (cid in cluster_ids) {     vox <- which(clusters == cid)     lap <- get_laplacian(get_local_adjacency(mask, vox))      # small (<= few hundred)     k <- min(k_per_cluster, length(vox))     vecs <- RSpectra::eigs_sym(lap, k = k, which = "SM")$vectors     for (cc in seq_len(k)) {       i[[length(i)+1]] <- vox       j[[length(j)+1]] <- rep(col_off + cc, length(vox))       x[[length(x)+1]] <- vecs[, cc]     }     col_off <- col_off + k   }   L <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = unlist(i), j = unlist(j), x = unlist(x),                             dims = c(sum(mask), col_off))   B <- as.matrix(X %*% L)   LatentNeuroVec(basis = Matrix::Matrix(B), loadings = L,                  space = neuroim2::space(mask), mask = mask) }

title: SlepianEtc Notes
text: Clustering vs Graph Coarsening: partition (supervoxels) makes Laplacian block-diagonal; coarsening builds multiscale coarse graph plus prolongation P lift eigenvectors (v_fine = P %*% v_coarse). Tradeoffs Clustering: extreme sparsity, embarrassingly parallel tiny eigenproblems, hard boundaries cut inter-parcel edges—great storage/compression; kills global gradients. Coarsening: preserves topology global gradients; lifting via P spreads support → denser loadings, heavier implementation (multigrid/Kron reduction). Fit fmrilatent: prefer supervoxel/cluster Slepians—maximally sparse loadings suit LatentNeuroVec; blockiness mitigated keeping k>1 modes per parcel (mean + gradients). “Soft supervoxel” compromise: keep supervoxel solves allow boundary voxels share weights across adjacent parcels, turning block-diagonal lightly banded loading matrix (smooths seams without dense blow-). Supervoxel constructor sketch Guideline: use clustering compression/denoising pipelines; consider coarsening smooth whole-brain gradients primary added density acceptable.
code: slepian_supervoxel_latent <- function(X, mask, n_supervoxels = 500, k_per_voxel = 3) {   sv <- neuroim2::cluster_voxels(mask, k = n_supervoxels, method = "slic")   i <- j <- x <- list(); col <- 0   for (id in sort(unique(sv[sv > 0]))) {     vox <- which(sv == id)     lap <- get_local_laplacian(mask, vox)     vecs <- RSpectra::eigs_sym(lap, k = min(k_per_voxel, length(vox)), which = "SM")$vectors     for (cc in seq_len(ncol(vecs))) {       i[[length(i)+1]] <- vox       j[[length(j)+1]] <- rep(col + cc, length(vox))       x[[length(x)+1]] <- vecs[, cc]     }     col <- col + ncol(vecs)   }   L <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = unlist(i), j = unlist(j), x = unlist(x),                             dims = c(sum(mask), col))   B <- as.matrix(X %*% L)   LatentNeuroVec(basis = B, loadings = L, space = neuroim2::space(mask),                  mask = mask, meta = list(method = "slepian_supervoxel")) }

title: Encoding workflows
text: Temporal specs project voxel’s time series onto shared set basis functions. data matrix X (time x voxels) becomes basis B (time x k) loadings L (voxels x k). B orthonormal, loadings simplify L = t(X) %*% B; otherwise encode() uses least-squares projection implied B, equivalent solving B’B. choose k control compression ratio.

title: Encoding workflows
text: Discrete prolate spheroidal sequences concentrate energy frequency band minimizing spectral leakage. Use resting-state data analysis focused specific frequency range. bandwidth parameter (Hz) tr (seconds) together determine normalized half-bandwidth W = bandwidth * tr. number well-concentrated tapers approximately 2 * n_time * W - 1; setting k lower gives heavier compression.
code: spec_slep <- spec_time_slepian(tr = 2, bandwidth = 0.08, k = 4) lat_slep <- encode(X, spec_slep, mask = mask_vol, materialize = "matrix")  # 4 basis vectors spanning the 0-0.08 Hz band dim(basis(lat_slep)) #> [1] 20  4  # Reconstruction error sqrt(mean((as.matrix(lat_slep) - X)^2)) #> [1] 0.8974354

title: Encoding workflows
text: discrete cosine transform provides orthogonal frequency components. fast parameter-free beyond choosing k — good default strong prior signal bandwidth.
code: lat_dct <- encode(X, spec_time_dct(k = 8), mask = mask_vol, materialize = "matrix") dim(basis(lat_dct)) #> [1] 20  8 sqrt(mean((as.matrix(lat_dct) - X)^2)) #> [1] 0.7783513

title: Encoding workflows
text: B-splines produce smooth, localized basis functions controllable flexibility. useful modeling slow drifts hemodynamic response, want smooth temporal structure without frequency-domain assumptions. degree parameter controls smoothness (3 = cubic, default). Set orthonormalize = TRUE (default) orthonormal columns, simplifies downstream linear algebra.
code: lat_bs <- encode(X, spec_time_bspline(k = 6, degree = 3), mask = mask_vol,                  materialize = "matrix") dim(basis(lat_bs)) #> [1] 20  6

title: Encoding workflows
text: three temporal encodings follow pattern. trade-spectral precision (Slepian), simplicity (DCT), localization (B-spline):
code: rmse <- function(lat) sqrt(mean((as.matrix(lat) - X)^2))  data.frame(   family = c("Slepian (k=4)", "DCT (k=8)", "B-spline (k=6)"),   k      = c(ncol(basis(lat_slep)), ncol(basis(lat_dct)), ncol(basis(lat_bs))),   rmse   = round(c(rmse(lat_slep), rmse(lat_dct), rmse(lat_bs)), 4) ) #>           family k   rmse #> 1  Slepian (k=4) 4 0.8974 #> 2      DCT (k=8) 8 0.7784 #> 3 B-spline (k=6) 6 0.8239

title: Encoding workflows
text: Spatial specs reduce number spatial locations projecting voxels onto set spatial atoms. roles reverse: loadings L (voxels x k) define spatial dictionary, temporal coefficients become C. orthonormal spatial dictionary C = X %*% L; non-orthonormal dictionaries encoder uses corresponding Gram solve.

title: Encoding workflows
text: Graph Slepian bases eigenvectors graph Laplacian, spectrally concentrated spatial clusters. spatial analog temporal DPSS sequences. k parameter sets number components per cluster; k_neighbors controls k-NN graph used spatial adjacency.
code: lat_sp <- encode(X, spec_space_slepian(k = 3, k_neighbors = 6),                  mask = mask_vol)

title: Encoding workflows
text: Heat wavelets approximate diffusion voxel graph multiple time scales, capturing local global spatial structure. scales parameter controls diffusion time scales (larger = smoother); order sets Chebyshev polynomial approximation order; threshold truncates small coefficients sparsity.
code: lat_heat <- encode(X,   spec_space_heat(scales = c(1, 2, 4, 8), order = 30, threshold = 1e-6),   mask = mask_vol )

title: Encoding workflows
text: HRBF places smooth Gaussian atoms data-driven centers. family gives explicit, interpretable spatial basis functions. sigma0 parameter controls atom width; levels controls hierarchy depth (levels = finer resolution); radius_factor sets atom spacing relative sigma.
code: lat_hrbf <- encode(X,   spec_space_hrbf(params = list(     sigma0 = 2, levels = 1,     radius_factor = 2.5, kernel_type = "gaussian"   )),   mask = mask_vol )

title: Encoding workflows
text: wavelet active encoder applies CDF 5/3 lifting wavelets along spatial axis, touching -mask voxels. exact (biorthogonal) fast — best choice speed-critical pipelines. Setting threshold > 0 zeroes small wavelet coefficients lossy compression. threshold = 0 transform exact.
code: lat_wav <- encode(X,   spec_space_wavelet_active(levels_space = 2, levels_time = 0, threshold = 0),   mask = mask_vol )  # Wavelet active returns an ImplicitLatent; reconstruct with predict() recon_wav <- predict(lat_wav) dim(recon_wav)

title: Encoding workflows
text: Parcel-local PCA computes per-cluster SVD build block-sparse spatial dictionary. parcel contributes k components. data-driven approach — loadings subject-specific. center parameter subtracts voxel means PCA (stored offset()); whiten = TRUE rescales scores unit variance.
code: lat_pca <- encode(X, spec_space_pca(k = 3, center = TRUE), mask = mask_vol,                   reduction = red)  # 4 parcels x 3 components = 12 total spatial atoms dim(loadings(lat_pca)) #> [1] 64 12

title: Encoding workflows
text: parcellation (atlas) want spatial dictionary across subjects, use parcel_basis_template(). default basis Laplacian eigenvectors — smooth functions voxel adjacency graph within parcel. training data needed. example uses one PCA component per parcel fast fully reproducible. Geometric templates use encoding surface: lift()-compatible basis spec works: basis_slepian() (default), basis_pca(), basis_heat_wavelet().
code: # Build template once from the shared reduction. tmpl <- parcel_basis_template(red, basis_pca(k = 1), data = X, center = TRUE) tmpl #> ParcelBasisTemplate #>   Basis family: spec_pca  #>   Atoms: 4  #>   Voxels: 64  #>   Parcels: 4  #>   Center at encode: TRUE  # Project each subject onto the shared dictionary lvec_s1 <- encode(X, spec_space_parcel(tmpl), mask = mask_vol)  # Loadings are identical across subjects; scores and offset vary dim(basis(lvec_s1))     # time x atoms #> [1] 20  4 dim(loadings(lvec_s1))  # voxels x atoms #> [1] 64  4 atlas <- neuroim2::ClusteredNeuroVol(mask_vol, parcel_map) tmpl_slepian <- parcel_basis_template(atlas, basis_slepian(k = 5)) lvec <- encode(X, spec_space_parcel(tmpl_slepian), mask = mask_vol)

title: Encoding workflows
text: spec_st() combines temporal spatial spec separable representation. Instead storing full reconstructed matrix, stores small core tensor decodes demand. Partial decoding main advantage separable encoding. reconstruct single time point region interest without paying cost full reconstruction. core tensor typically tiny (k_time x k_space), storage minimal regardless original data size.
code: lat_st <- encode(X,   spec_st(     time  = spec_time_bspline(k = 4, degree = 3),     space = spec_space_hrbf(params = list(       sigma0 = 2, levels = 0, radius_factor = 2.5, seed = 42L     ))   ),   mask = mask_vol )  # Full reconstruction full <- predict(lat_st) dim(full) #> [1] 20 64  # Partial: only time points 1-5 partial <- predict(lat_st, time_idx = 1:5) dim(partial) #> [1]  5 64  # Partial: only voxels in an ROI roi <- array(FALSE, dim = c(4, 4, 4)) roi[1:2, 1:2, 1:2] <- TRUE roi_data <- predict(lat_st, roi_mask = roi) dim(roi_data) #> [1] 20  8

title: Encoding workflows
text: latent_factory() builds spec calls encode() one step. handy quick experiments: Family strings follow <axis>_<method> convention. Available strings underlying specs: older <method>_<axis> names ("dct_time", "slepian_space", …) still work aliases, existing code break. Extra arguments ... forwarded spec constructor. two-step pattern (spec encode()) gives control; factory shortcut defaults suffice. Note B-spline temporal encoding factory — use spec_time_bspline() encode() directly.
code: lat_f <- latent_factory("time_dct", x = X, mask = mask_vol, k = 8,                         materialize = "matrix") dim(basis(lat_f)) #> [1] 20  8

title: Encoding workflows
text: materialize argument encode() controls bases stored internally: "handle" (default): lazy object generates basis columns demand. Saves memory basis large need partial reconstruction. "matrix": explicit dense matrix. Faster repeated full reconstructions since basis precomputed. produce identical numerical results. Choose "handle" memory matters; choose "matrix" call .matrix() series() repeatedly.

title: Diffusion Wavelets (Section 2.3 & Figure 2)
text: Goal: build data-adaptive multiscale bases graph/manifold diffusing Markov operator T compressing range dyadic powers filter high-frequency detail. Dyadic powers: examine T^(2^j); j grows, diffusion spreads numerical rank drops. Compression/basis update: scale, run modified, rank-revealing QR current operator representation find coarse orthonormal scaling basis phi_{j+1} within tolerance epsilon. Scaling functions stored “extended” back original basis phi_0. Wavelets orthogonal complement. Downsampling operator: project/square compressed operator form T^(2^{j+1}) new basis, iterating space collapses (rank 1 stopping rule).

title: Diffusion Wavelets (Section 2.3 & Figure 2)
code: def DiffusionWavelets(T, epsilon):     # Inputs: T (N x N transition/similarity matrix), epsilon (compression precision)     # Outputs: extended scaling bases phis, extended wavelet bases psis (each in terms of phi_0)     phi_0 = I_N                          # Dirac basis on original nodes     current_T = T                        # [T]_phi0^phi0     extended_phis = [phi_0]              # [phi_j]_phi0     extended_psis = []     j = 0     while size(current_T) > 1:           # or other stop (rank collapse / max_J)         Q, R = ModifiedQR(current_T, epsilon)        # Q ~ [phi_{j+1}]_phi_j ; R ~ [T^(2^j)]_phi_j^phi_{j+1}         phi_next_global = Q @ extended_phis[j]       # [phi_{j+1}]_phi0         extended_phis.append(phi_next_global)          Q_wavelet, _ = ModifiedQR(I - Q @ Q.T, epsilon)  # wavelet complement in phi_j coordinates         psi_next_global = Q_wavelet @ extended_phis[j]   # [psi_j]_phi0         extended_psis.append(psi_next_global)          compressed_T = R @ Q                          # [T^(2^j)]_phi_{j+1}^phi_{j+1}         current_T = compressed_T @ compressed_T       # square for dyadic step: [T^(2^{j+1})]_phi_{j+1}^phi_{j+1}         j += 1     return extended_phis, extended_psis

title: Diffusion Wavelets (Section 2.3 & Figure 2)
text: Bottleneck: deterministic rank-revealing QR dense N x N matrices O(N^3) diffusion causes fill-. Intractable many-thousand–million node graphs. Remedy: randomized rank-revealing QR (Halko–Martinsson–Tropp style) approximate column space factoring. Draw Gaussian Omega shape n x (k+p). Form sketch Y = @ Omega (fast sparse/implicit ). Orthonormalize Y -> Q = qr(Y). Project small matrix B = Q.T @ . Factor small B deterministic QR/SVD: U_small, R_small = qr(B). Reconstruct basis Q_final = Q @ U_small, giving ≈ Q_final @ R_small. Complexity drops toward O(N * k^2) O(N^2 log k), heavy lift highly parallelizable multiply @ Omega.

title: Diffusion Wavelets (Section 2.3 & Figure 2)
text: Short answer: vanilla DWT (basic randomized QR) scale 100K-node small-world connectome unless extra constraints added. Fill-small-world topology: degree ~100 gives ~10K neighbors T^2 near-full coverage T^4, making T^(2^j) dense (~80 GB 100K x 100K) QR O(1e15) FLOPs. Slow spectral decay: connectome spectra decay slowly, epsilon-driven truncation may still require tens thousands basis vectors (e.g., 40K), making QR 100K x 40K matrix infeasible. Constraints make workable - Never form T^2 explicitly: evaluate products Y = T(T Omega) cost scales nnz(T) rather N^2. - Aggressive sparsification: threshold small entries (e.g., < 1e-5) compression prevent density growth. - Fix target rank (e.g., 2K–5K) instead epsilon-based rank discovery; accept loss high-frequency detail stay tractable. Sketch scalable loop (brain-sized) Effect: Figure 2 flow blow first squaring; constrained randomized path can finish realistic hardware capping rank keeping operations implicit.
code: def Scalable_Brain_DWT(T_sparse, target_rank=2000, oversample=20, max_scales=...):     current_T = T_sparse  # 100K x 100K sparse (~10M nnz)     for _ in range(max_scales):         Omega = randn(current_T.shape[0], target_rank + oversample)         Y = current_T.dot(current_T.dot(Omega))          # implicit T^2 @ Omega, sparse-dense         Q, _ = np.linalg.qr(Y, mode="reduced")           # tall-skinny QR         B = current_T.dot(Q)                             # sparse-dense multiply         T_compressed = B.T.dot(B)                        # small dense (target_rank x target_rank)         T_compressed[np.abs(T_compressed) < 1e-5] = 0    # enforce sparsity if desired         save_basis(Q)                                    # store basis analog of [phi_{j+1}]_phi_j         current_T = T_compressed         if current_T.shape[0] < target_rank:             break
